chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah from Aban ibn Uthman from Ismail ibn al-Fadl who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the fabrication (iftira') upon the Ahl al-Zimma and the People of the Book. Would the Muslim be whipped the Hadd penalty regarding the fabrication against them? He (peace be upon him) said: No, but he would be reprimanded (mu'azzar).

key_terms.أَهْلِ الذِّمَّةِ: People of the covenant (non-Muslims living under Muslim rule)
key_terms.أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ: People of the Book (Jews and Christians)
key_terms.يُجْلَدُ الْحَدَّ: To be whipped the fixed Hadd penalty
key_terms.يُعَزَّرُ: To be given a discretionary Ta'zir punishment

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for fabricating claims against non-Muslims in Islamic law?
ai.summary: Imam Jafar al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between the fixed Hadd penalty and discretionary Ta'zir, ruling that fabricating claims against Ahl al-Zimma warrants the latter, reflecting the flexibility of judicial discretion in maintaining social order. This ruling underscores the importance of protecting the legal rights and dignity of non-Muslim minorities within the Islamic polity, ensuring justice is administered with nuance rather than rigid application of fixed penalties. It highlights the scholarly tradition of differentiating between specific divine limits and the ruler's or judge's authority to adapt punishments to the context of the offense.
